name: IPPR (Institute for Public Policy Research)
detail: Statement of 2025 found concerns taxing income from wealth (capital gains alignment) and "stealth taxes over wealth taxes"; no call for a tax on net wealth found. Earlier IPPR work covers property and inheritance taxes. Re-check IPPR publications for an explicit wealth tax recommendation.

name: Fairness Foundation
detail: Its taxing-wealth pages are JavaScript-rendered and could not be read; a search found only a general statement on progressive taxation, no wealth tax figure. Retry with a different route (publications, press releases).

name: New Economics Foundation
detail: SUPERSEDED in R013: NEF added as an actor (2023 analysis with Tax Justice UK, grade B). NEF-hosted pages found are a guest blog (Women's Budget Group, 22 Sep 2025) that describes a 2% over £10m tax as a popular option, and a 17 Jul 2026 essay by Liam Byrne MP. Neither is an NEF institutional statement. NEF 2023 costing (with Tax Justice UK) reported in secondary sources only. Look for an NEF report or press release.

name: EDM 1037 Wealth tax and social security reform (Eastwood, 2025)
detail: Motion text calls for "tax increases for the super-wealthy" without referring to a tax on wealth; its 9 signatories were not added on this motion.

name: Mark Robinson (Commonwealth Human Ecology Council, Chair)
detail: Signed the Bond letter of 27 Feb 2025 (H0013) but an actor named Mark Robinson already exists from the Proud to Pay list; not known whether they are the same person, so no second row was added.

name: Supporters of Scottish Parliament motion S7M-00249 Wealth Taxation for Public Services (4 Jun 2026)
detail: Motion agreed 84-28 but its text welcomes a private jet tax and mansion tax (excluded designs), says Scotland has limited scope for additional wealth taxation, and endorses exploring further steps; amendments (Harvie, Schmulian, Hoy, Marra, Rennie) contain no call for a tax on net wealth (Harvie: Amazon tax via non-domestic rates, property tax reform). No MSPs added from this vote.

name: Aditya Chakrabortty
detail: Guardian column of 20 Nov 2025 calls wealth tax proposals a pantomime of pseudo-radicalism (as quoted in a Guardian letters reply). Not a supporter.

name: Charlie Mullins
detail: Founder and chairman of WeFix; July 2026 post argues against demanding that other successful people pay more (Patriotic Millionaires). Not a supporter.

name: Richard Murphy
detail: Chartered accountant, Tax Research UK. Generally argues against a separate annual wealth tax and prefers closing loopholes on capital gains, dividends and inheritance (user correction; his July 2025 blog line "tax wealth properly" had been logged as grade B in error).
